full_text: Do not buy if you intend to use with the iPhone 6+. This Gimbal stabilizer was the 1st of its kind that Ive ever purchased for use with a smart phone. It was advertised to work with larger smart phones such as the iPhone 6+, and also with the go Pro. Over the course of 2 months Ive taken this out to use on a trip with my iPhone 6+. All of my footage comes out a little bit crooked. Crooked to the left (so the footage looks like its going downhill to the right). It doesnt matter how I balance the unit, it starts out looking okay, but with more and more use the footage leans more and more to the left. I ruled out batteries, and charge level by purchasing extras to swap in. I ruled out improper balancing by even overcompensating for it to hopefully tilt more towards the right to try to correct for the tendency of the unit to lean left. Ive even thought about modifying the cradle to lean more towards the right as the best solution while I was using it abroad. Unfortunately, as I briefly mentioned, the lean to the left is not always consistent and will vary with more and more use. It was at that point and realization that my trying to jury rig my own solution would not work -- that I contacted customer service. I received a prompt reply saying that I can RMA it and possibly have the servos adjusted after inspection. That really didn't do me any good because I was overseas in Asia. Coming back from the trip I decided to try another unit. Same issue: completely worthless with the iPhone 6+ no matter what way I balanced. Even trying to overcompensate for the balance by putting more weight on the right-hand side in hopes of getting a level shot. I have given up hope. I do not recommend this Gimbel stabilizer for the iPhone 6+. It does not work as advertised. On the flipside, I did use it with the GoPro 4 with the mount which was sold separately, and it works. The rest of the features and functionality are as advertised. Its very easy to use, and I think that is its best feature. As far as durability is concerned, the unit does not feel like it would last as well as one would expect were it to be labeled professional gear. The rubberized finish on the unit is likely to wear off with any moderate amount of use. In the month that Ive used it (sparingly), I see the finished coming off already in certain parts of the unit. The 2nd month, I didn't really use it much at all since all the footage was crooked. One further thing that I didn't like about the minute was that swapping between the cradles involved taking out the included hex wrench and removing some screws to switch mounts and cradles. If you are intending to use this only with one type of device, let it be the go Pro, and you won't have any of the inconveniences of removing screws, snapping the cradles in and out, adjusting the weight(s), and possibly losing said screws.

full_text: Marked as one of the top 2017 budget dash cams and a good long-term investment... This camera had been reviewed by several tech articles noting it to be one of the top budget or affordable dash cams for 2017 at the time I was reviewing different devices. The design is pretty solid with it's zinc alloy metal exterior and is reasonably compact and not bulky for use when mounting to the front windshield. The loop recording on this device is nice and with the G-sensor video lock feature that you can enable-- you can prevent important footage from being erased before having a chance to download the video capture to a computer. Unlike some dash cams on the market-- out of the box you get everything you need to set up the device in your vehicle and start recording. Installation is pretty easy, you don't need to worry about wiring-- just plug the unit's power cable into your 12V cigarette lighter and use the included mounting cable clips and camera suction mount to secure into place. I did contact the company because the USB microSD card adapter (also included in the box) for the 32GB microSD card had been damaged somehow during the shipping process. They were able to send me a replacement quickly once we were in communication about the matter. This is a nice item to have versus unhooking the camera to directly connect to the computer to pull off video files. The fact that the camera itself comes with a decent microSD card of the highest space capacity that can be read by the dash cam is a definite plus. Many dash cams I researched didn't provide the record-able media and would have resulted in a secondary purchase just to use the device. Overall this camera has been sturdy and easy to make use of in my daily commute drive. It may not have all the newest features of more recent cameras, but provides a good amount of features at a reasonable price. Well worth the investment for a simple dash cam that's easy to set up and use right out of the box.

full_text: Great features but poor design and poor thermal handling. Purchased this item as my first home theater receiver. I've never owned one before. I opted for this due to the price point (Currently at $260). I spent countless hours researching and learning how to properly setup a home theater system. I paired this receiver (new, not a refurbished one) with the Energy 5.1 Take Classic system. I utilize 1 HDMI input (xbox), the radio and bluetooth from my phones and computers to stream music. I also utilized USB drives to play music as well. First and foremost - this item will regularly shut off when you play music for an extended period of time (by extended, I mean more than 10-15 minutes). The item goes into 'protect' mode. The receiver isn't blocked with other equipment that could lead to overheating, but there is absolutely no reason for this receiver to go into such a mode after 10 minutes of playback. The denon manual says this happens when the temperatures rise and it's a feature to stop the receiver from incurring actual damage - this makes sense. What DOESN'T make sense is, I use XBOX for Netflix, HBO GO, other video apps...and the volume needs to be at 50-55 to be audible in a small living room. For decent playback of music, volume needs to be at 55-65. Volume @ 70 is about 3/4ths of the total volume output of the receiver - and I tested this by playing music (nothing bass-heavy) for 10 minutes at volume 70 and at the 11 minute mark it went into protect mode. I don't understand why you can't hear anything from volume 1-40, but if you go over volume 60 you have to worry about thermal / heating issues? This isn't an isolated issue, there are a dozen+ complaints with this same exact issue. This is a manufacturing issue and is due to poor design. Putting the volume/thermal issues aside, Bluetooth decided to stop working altogether 3 weeks into owning the receiver. I've powered off all the devices and attempted to re-pair to no avail. Again, the other reviews here on Amazon echo that this seems to be a common issue with this Denon receiver. Luckily Amazon is working with me and sending me a replacement. Additional thoughts and details: Typical consumers may find the need of an app or controller to configure and change this a little but too much, but remotely technical folks will likely be *very* happy. I'd recommend it for sure.

full_text: Buyer Beware  There are 2 different versions of this camera with the same model #! I went through several different cameras before finally deciding that this one had all the features and easy functionality that I required. So I decided to buy 2 more of the eventual 6 I planned to install. Sadly, I did not have time to install the second two cameras until well after the return policy had expired. I say sadly as the second two cameras I received are a different version of the same camera! The differences are serious enough that they should have different model #s in my book, thus my Buyer Beware review title! The first one I received was a Version 2 and the second 2 were version 1s. And based on the ancient firmware in the second 2 cams (one needed 3 rounds of firmware upgrades to catch up!) these were also probably repacks of some type and not even new merchandise I would totally dog this review with one star for the Foscam rip-off swap out, but I was an idiot and didn't check the boxes of the second two cameras when I received them, so I am accepting the blame But be warned! The Version 2 cam has MUCH newer firmware available (and is thus, in theory, safer.) It also has additional features from the Version 1 cams. I don't know all of them, but the 2 main ones that I am REALLY missing is that the V2 can send push alerts to your iPhone via the Foscam program if you have it set up for motion or sound detection alarms. The V1s don't support motion phone push alerts (although you can email yourself an alert) and the V1s also don't support audio alerts (alarms) at all! [I would have returned the V1s immediately if I had known...] Interestingly, however, the V1 cams have a better picture and have MUCH better night vision than the V2 does. One of the ways you can spot the difference between the two versions is that on the V2 the IR LEDs are covered by a semitransparent cover and you cant see the IR LEDs on the front, and on the V1s you can see them. I suspect that this cover is why the night vision on the V2 is worse than the V1. (I uploaded a pic of the two types side by side.) When I say the night vision is worse, yes I do mean that the V2 is not as bright in night vision mode, but the difference does not stop there. I placed a V1 and a V2 in the EXACT same spot (by my router as you need to upgrade the firmware via Ethernet) and changing nothing else in the environment, both the V1s gave me a color picture, but the V2 decided the lighting was not bright enough and switched to Black & White night vision only mode. I was curious, so I went into the settings and manually turned off the Auto IR mode on the V2 and it then gave me the same color picture as the V1s did in Auto mode (Yes I had all three cams set to the same settings and had auto-night-vision enabled on all, and all had the latest firmware.) So it is kind of a tradeoff... The V1 has a better picture and works better in the dark. It also seems to pan slightly faster (in fast mode) than the V2. But the V2 has more features, more up to date firmware, and looks a tad better due to the LED cover. I frankly wish I could have a V1 with the V2 feature set as I don't care about the IR cover and care more that the picture is better on the V1s (not significantly but noticeably.) Also, FYI, if you get a V1, download the software from the Foscam web site manually. If your V1 has new enough firmware loaded in it to have the feature, using the download the latest firmware button in the camera management system downloaded v118 and I got v119 when I downloaded it manually from Foscam. One of my V1s was so old that the only way to get the firmware software was Foscams web site, and when I was done I noticed that the V1 I did manually had newer software than the V1 I upgraded with the button, so I did the other V1 with the manual firmware. No clue what the difference is, if any. As for the rest of it, overall I like the cams, I love the zoom feature, the picture is good, the cam was easy to set up (although it was time consuming to do so many firmware upgrades,) and the Foscam software on my iPhone is easy to use and get working outside of your local network. Both the V1 and the V2 were MUCH easier than the Amcrest HD units I tried, BTW. So Foscam rip-off, out-of-date, repacked, merchandise aside, I am giving them 4 stars anyway

full_text: Can be a great router, with some modifications and good technical knowledge This could be a great router, with a caveat. See below for positives and negatives. Positives: First of all, this router can be very fast, IF all you use it for is wireless. The coverage from a high open area in the living room is most of my 1/3 acre of property, inside and out. Negatives: However, much of my equipment requires a strong LAN setup, and this is a major failure of the v2 version of this router. Windows 10 really struggles to find an IP address via LAN with this device, even when directly connected via high-quality Cat6 or Cat7 cables. Thinking I might have a bad router, I put in a help ticket. I first talked to James in tech support via email and he suggested I get an RMA. However, the RMA department was slow to respond for several days. They eventually shipped me a replacement router overnight and without charge due to the delay, so I ended up getting the replacement at about the same time as I should have if it had been sent ground when approved. When the 2nd router arrived, it too did the exact same thing. It took about 15 minutes after any restart to get get a LAN connection. This router does NOT handle changes in the cable modem's base IP address well at all on the stock firmware. Even the most updated firmware at the time I got the replacement, the delay was excruciating when I had work to get done. Solution:All of the above said, however, there is hope for this router. Install DD-WRT on this device and it shines. I lost about 5% of my overall wireless / LAN speed (as I was warned in the DD-WRT forums I would), but the stability, reliability, and automatic creation of the LAN when the PC restarted was so worth it. I still get almost 150 mbps down and 25 mbps up with a Motorola Surfboard 6183 modem on TimeWarner's 100 / 5 service. The bit problem with giving this thing more stars is that while I had little issue using DD-WRT to fix the problems, TP-Link is limiting the ability to use this fix in future firmwares, so if you get one that's updated and locked, you are stuck. Additionally, only 25-30% of the people ordering this are going to be able to install and set up DD-WRT (if that many), so to recommend this to the average user would not be honest. Again, if you just have 10-12 wireless devices and no need for a wired LAN, this would be a great router. I've never had any wifi issues with either the 1st or 2nd router I've had. full_text: Fantastic 4K UHD Passive 3D Smart TV - about the only option for this at this size. This TV is stunning. What isn't stunning is LG in general. The first TV we received had what appeared to be a manufacturing defect in the projection plane of the TV. I say apparent because there was no damage to the packaging, the screen, or the back of the TV - however when it was turned on the image had fixed vertical and horizontal lines coming out of an area on the right side of the screen which was black and had the appearance of a cracked screen - though external screen was not cracked. Luckily we bought this from a very good seller (Pro Audio Video) who quickly sent us a replacement (as soon as shipper picked up the broken TV we had a tracking number for the replacement the next day). Tech Review: The screen is very clear, very bright, and fantastic to watch anything from TV to the latest 3D content on. It auto scales all video to 4K - obviously the higher the resolution you start with the better the result - but even up-scaling 480i video looks fantastic. It wants to be the center of your entertainment system - controlling your other units via HDMI Control connections. However it can easily be configured down to work as basically the display for a larger system without too much issue. There are sufficient configuration settings to meet all your needs with relatively simple and self explanatory descriptions. ACR works well for the apps you want to control through the TV. LG support assures us all three HDMI ports are HDCP 2.2 compliant - they were unable to address an issue we had with an older Sony 400 Disk DVD changer which required an older revision of HDCP over HDMI. If you are one of these people (and I used to be, so no judgment), please do yourself a favor and give these headphones a chance. The sound is not flat and boring, it's bright and clean, and don't sound muffled at any point. The bass is perfectly balanced and neither under nor over powering. Aside from the sound, the build quality is excellent and you have more than enough foam and rubber tips to choose from. Normally, I have a tough time fitting in-ears as my right ear is shaped differently than my left. I didn't have that issue with these, and they sit comfortably in my ears. I certainly wouldn't run or exercise with these though, they are a bit heavy on the ears for that. But for regular walking around, or sitting at a desk, they are close to perfect. So why not 5 stars? The mic and remote are not very good. I had a problem with my original pair which was faulty. The buttons would perform the wrong function when I pressed them. For example, I would try to change the song and it would get louder, or I would try to make it lower and the song would change. Quite an interesting malfunction, and a frustrating one for a $100 pair of headphones. I reached out to them directly and they shipped me a new pair within a week. Although that problem is fixed, one problem that I have even with this new pair is the mic quality. Sometimes my iPhone doesn't even recognize the mic and I find myself screaming until I realize I have to talk into the phone. Again, not problems that $100 headphones should have. I literally avoid taking phone calls when using these. It's not my phone, because I also own a pair of Brainwaves Delta which work perfectly fine (for $20 ish I might add- those are fantastic if you can't really splurge on earbuds at the moment). Aside from that, know that your money will be well spent if you're deciding to upgrade. I wear them for upwards of 8 hours a day between listening to music at work and an hour commute to and from work each day. They are comfortable enough to use for that much time each day. If you're deciding between these and the quad drivers, you will not get double the sound quality with those, and the improvements are only nominal compared to the leap these make from other pairs in the same price point. Opt for these and I don't think you'l be disappointed.

full_text: Freezing/Hard Lock Hello, I've been having a freezing problem right from the start with this processor on my new Skylake build. I put together this system last month, in January 2016. All parts are brand new and fresh install of windows 10. System: Case: Corsair Carbide Series Air 540 High Airflow ATX Cube Case CPU: i7 6700k Skylake 4.00GHZ GPU: MSI GTX 980 Ti Motherboard: ASUS ROG MAXIMUS VIII HERO SSD: OCZ Storage Vector 180 Series 960GB SSHD: Seagate 4TB PSU: EVGA SuperNOVA GOLD 850W RAM: Corsair Vengeance LPX 32GB (4 x 8GB) DDR4 DRAM 2400MHz OS: Windows 10 64-bit Thermal Paste: Arctic Silver In the off-chance anything might be helpful, and because it's starting to frustrate the crap out of me, here's a dump of everything I've learned so far about my particular issue, and other things that could possibly be related. Alright, so I am experiencing complete system freezes at random moments. Screen remains displaying the moment of the freeze. Also, speakers will occasionally play a harsh deafening sound. Basically, the speakers remain outputting the last tone of whatever was being played at the moment of the freeze, if there was one. The louder the volume is turned up and depending on what tone is being played, it can be very unpleasant and almost deafening if using a headset. With that being said, if the speakers were silent of the time of crash, there will be no "screech of death" since no tone is being played. At first I thought it was an issue with the GPU, sound card, motherboard, etc. Issues pointed towards my audio drivers conflicting. After disabling all audio devices except the speakers and updating drivers the problem still occurs. Problem occurs using both headset and speakers. After a ton of research and troubleshooting I have finally narrowed it down to the new skylake CPU's. I am trying everything to make my PC stable and the longest I've gone without a freeze is 24 hours, maybe 2 days. Sometimes I will get 3-4 crashes in a day if I'm playing a lot. So here is what I've tried so far: Updating various drivers/BIOS. No effect even with the most recent BIOS dated January 7th, 2016. I have also tested the memory using memtest86 returning no errors.. Problem has been reproduced on many storage devices. SSD, SSHD, and HDD. One user even reported freezes during USB flash drive boot-ups. The problem has been reproduced using many different Mobo and RAM manufactures. I personally have tested both corsair and G.skill. Others have reported using crucial, gskill, and corsair with different sizes, frequencies, and mobos. Everyone is getting the same freezes. I am close to RMA'ing just to mess around with some different hardware but I honestly don't think it will fix the issue since others have already tried that. Also, Corsair and G.skill is some of the best memory on the market so I really don't think that memory is to blame here. This has also been brushed off as an overheating issue by some users. I suspected it was overheating since I was crashing at around 70 Celsius while playing taxing games like Ark:Survival on max settings. That's what you do when you build a new rig, right? Then I tested it playing Heroes of the Storm and other low end games. Problem persists even at 40-50 degrees Celsius.. So it can't possibly be an overheating issue. Others have showed similar low temps while freezing occurs. I have also already noted that some users are freezing while idle. Lately I keep Speccy up 24/7 just to see what my temps are during freezes. Temperatures do not seem to correlate with the freezing. So I already mentioned I was able to reproduce the crashing in many different applications, mostly video games like Heroes of the Storm, League of Legends, Smite etc just to ensure it wasn't a problem with any one application. I have yet to freeze during idle, however my system sleeps after 30 minutes so that is probably why I haven't experienced a freeze yet while idling. I am going to turn off sleep mode tonight just to see if I crash while idling. I have ran prime95 tests and pushed my CPU to 100% many times without returning any errors. Also, freezing occurs while playing the most taxing games such as Ark:Survival as well as low end video games such as League of Legends. I've reinstalled windows 10 as a fresh install even though this was a new build and it was already a new partition. Freezing still occurs. Also worth noting that it tends to happen at the most crucial moments of the game(hehe). I have read many posts of people blaming it on a bad batch of CPU's. After doing a ton of research I have found the issue to persist in about 75% of the new Skylake processors. Some enthusiasts have already RMA'd their CPU's two, three, some even 50 times over again with the crashing still occurring. One user made a very strong point worth noting: A big clue is that this is hard locks (not a software lock). You know this because interrupts have stopped.. the system is dead in an unnatural way actually. These are caused by very specific things (usually a race condition of some sort) and usually at a very low level (not software controlled in any way). Yes it can be a failed setup of hardware (bad driver register settings) but its not a software code execution failure, there was no line of code that died in this moment. This points directly to faulty hardware, not a software or driver issue, however it is worth mentioning that a BIOS update may fix it in the future. This is all speculation and doesn't really point towards a fix. However, If I am right, you should all wait a bit longer before RMA'ing since you will not get "fixed" versions until the next gen is released. The most frustrating part of this issue is that it can occur anywhere from 30 mins to 12 hours into a session. It is just really random and almost rare enough for me to just ignore. Extremely unpredictable. However, spending so much money on a new Skylake build I expect flawless performance. Hopefully we can get this issue resolved. I really don't feel like RMA'ing any more parts or downgrading to 5th gen. To anyone with the same issue, please let me know if you find a fix. I will update with any new information. Good luck. Update: Some are blaming bad batch of CPU's. Here is my batch: #L539B636 Also, it passed in Intel Processor Diagnostic Tool Update2: After about a month of troubleshooting I've finally got a stable system. Not even sure what fixed it honestly because I've tried so many solutions. I recently overclocked the CPU and raised the voltages of my RAM in BIOS so I'm pretty sure that's what fixed the crashes. I will update if I crash/freeze again but so far it's been a week with no issues so I think we are good. update3: Started Crashing again after playing some Ark and Black Desert Online this week. I crash about once or twice a day. I play for about 8 hours a day. This really needs to get fixed. I think I am done tinkering with RAM voltages and all this BIOS crap I'm just going to load default and possibly purchase a new CPU. Update4: I finally gave up and ordered a new processor. I down graded to i7 5820 haswell. I'm about 3 months in with no crashes or freezing so the issue was definitely the processor. I'm a little disappointed but at least now my system is stable.

full_text: Fluance offers best bang for the buck - great as larger bookshelf or full frequency satellite speakers! Best in price range! Fluance is a company that gained my attention, lost my attention, then gained it back again... plus they've got great personal customer service and stand behind their products... And as more people move away from bluetooth speakers to wifi/voice activated home stereos, there's a lot of value to be found in their product line. (I tried Fluance's bluetooth speaker which also was among the best but wasn't getting the true stereo separation and power I craved - hence I dusted off my old Onkyo receiver and set about to finding new speakers to pair them to for a kickass Alexa wifi voice controlled music on demand system!) These SXBPs - basically the dual directional speakers where you get 4 speakers for the price of two - have a great frequency range and although they're not going to rattle your windows, they convey the lows and highs better than most speakers out there for 4x the price of these These are part of a quadraphonic set up for me with another set of speakers carrying the low lows and the high highs - with these slated to send stereo sound into two separate rooms - but I'd still recommend these as stand alone budget bookshelf speakers that would blow away anything else at this price point. Sadly these are discontinued, yet they match the larger Fluance XLBP frequency range of 60Hz - 20KHz but for half the price (though the XLBP has better quality speaker cones) - meanwhile the smaller AVBP2 is probably best suited solely as satellite speakers for a multi speaker system that handles the lows and highs elsewhere But in my opinion these are some of the best, most versatile bookshelf/bipolar speakers out there. The sound is very very clean and with a full frequency response. Until Fluance comes out with something else in this size and price point, should you be lucky enough to still find these at bargain prices, snatch them up - they'll always have use and you won't be disappointed!

full_text: Causes Windows Explorer to freeze intermittently, and the hard drive will unmount and remount itself randomly. This is sad. I researched 4 highly rated USB to IDE/SATA adapters, and finally decided on this StarTech USB 2.0 to SATA IDE Adapter (USB2SATAIDE). Unfortunately, this is not a good product. I used this product on a Windows XP system with an old IDE hard drive. I connected the AC adapter to the drive (and waited 20 seconds for it to fully spin up like a StarTech customer service rep said in another review), and then I connected the USB cable to the computer. Each partition on the hard drive mounted as a separate drive in Windows (I saw the Autoplay popup for each drive). It seemed to be working. However, as I clicked around the directories on the hard drive in Windows Explorer, sometimes Explorer would freeze for 5-15 seconds before it finally listed the contents of a directory. This happened several times as I was clicking around all the directories on the hard drive. Very annoying. Then I decided to do hard drive surface scan, and during the scan, Windows unmounted the hard drive and re-mounted it. I could see the drive letters disappear in Explorer, and then they re-appeared and the Autoplay popups appeared again. Not good! I disconnected all the cables and reconnected them, and I encountered the same problems as before - occasional freezing in Windows Explorer and then the drives unmounting and re-mounting. You don't want the drive to be unmounting during a file transfer - that will cause data corruption. I thought maybe it was a problem with that particular hard drive, so I got another one of my old IDE drives and connected that one. Same problem - occasional freezing in Explorer and eventually the drive unmounted and remounted itself. I thought the StarTech USB adapter was defective at that point, so I had Amazon send me a replacement. I connected my old IDE hard drive to the replacement adapter, and same thing - freezes in Explorer and eventually the drive unmounted and remounted itself. This adapter is a poor product. I will have to try out one of the other brands that I researched - either Sabrent or Cable Unlimited.

(For those with dSLR's, if jiggling is a problem, you can also lock up your mirror, which should help reduce vibration) -Bulb mode: This is the kind of shot where movement kills the photo. Having an off-camera bulb mode is great. -Timer mode: This allows you to create a delay of up to 59 seconds, then fire a number of photos (1-99). Again, a great way to stabilize your camera. -Schedule mode: This allows you to specify a delay, then a program of [focus-shoot-interval x Number of Photos], then an interval before you repeat the program, along with a number of times to repeat (1-infinite). The other issue I had is that the manual can be difficult to understand since it appears to be a translation. No real complaint; it's more than I could do! The LED indicator will light green and the receiver will light up. The camera will remain in focus status until you release the button, or fully press it to take a picture. 3. To shoot, fully press the shutter button. The LED indicator will momentarily light red and the receiver will momentarily light up while you camera takes the shot. CONTINUOUS SHOOTING: 1. With the device powered ON, move the function to the continuous shooting icon by pressing the left or right buttons. 2. To focus, half-press the shutter button. The LED indicator will light green and the receiver will light up. The camera will remain in focus status until you release the button, or fully press it to take a picture. 3. To shoot, fully press the shutter button. The LED indicator will light red for as long as you hold the shutter. The receiver will also light up. The camera will continue to shoot for as long as you hold the shutter button. 4. Camera settings: a. Your camera should be in continuous mode. b. If your camera is in single-shot mode, it may only take a single picture. c. If your camera is in BULB mode, it may hold open the shutter for as long as you hold the shutter button. This can result in over- or under-exposure. d. If you camera is in timer mode, it may shoot a single delayed picture, or shoot several pictures in the delayed timer mode. BULB SHOOTING: 1. With the device powered ON, move the function to the BULB shooting icon by pressing the left or right buttons. 2. To focus, half-press the shutter button. The LED indicator will light green and the receiver will light up. The camera will remain in focus status until you release the button, or fully press it to take a picture. 3. To shoot, fully press the shutter button. The LED indicator will flash red. The transmitter is sending a continuous shoot signal. While the shutter is open, a timer will display showing the exposure time count. 4. Press the shutter button again. The transmitter will stop sending the shoot signal, and the camera will close the shutter. The LED will go out, and the display will show the total time the shutter was open. 5. Camera settings: a. Put the camera in BULB mode. b. In single mode, the camera will only take a single, normal shot. c. In burst mode, the camera will shoot continuously. d. In timer mode, the camera will take a single delayed picture. DELAYED SHOOTING: 1. The Delay mode will allow you to take a number of shots after a specified delay. 2. With the device powered ON, move the function to the timer icon by pressing the left or right buttons. 3. Press the SET button to enter the delay time until the first shot is taken. Press the SET button to lock in your settings. 6. To focus, half-press the shutter button. The LED indicator will light green and the receiver will light up. The camera will remain in focus status until you release the button, or fully press it to take a picture. 7. Fully press the shutter button to start the sequence. During the delay, the LED will rapidly flash red until the first shot. 8. For each shot, the LED will flash green during focusing and red during shooting. full_text: Disappointed.  Wish I'd gone with SanDisk or Samsung... TL;DR This drive, no matter what enclosure it is put in, periodically draws up to 1.35A of power through the USB port. That's more power draw than 2 external, physical hard drives (2.5" drives with spinning platters). This is not a drive to be used with laptops. They simply cannot support that kind of power draw and will eventually end up disconnecting this drive. Sooner or later that will lead to corrupted data. STAY AWAY!! Update: 11/3/2017 I just discovered something else negative about this drive. It draws a ridiculous amount of power in spurts. I've been trying to use this as a mobile drive, thinking I can put media on at home and then get decent read-only speeds out of it for playback. But I also wanted to be able to hook it up to a hub connected to my 12" MacBook, and that's where I ran into problems. I got a nice USB-C hub (OWC), but found when I connected this ADATA and a WD 2Tb My Passport (physical hard drive) the drives would disconnect sporadically and I wouldn't be able to copy a file from one to the other. I sent the hub back to OWC on an RMA, but had the same problem with the replacement. So I put testers on both of the hard drives and the hub to see if I could figure out what was drawing too much. I figured the problem would be the My Passport, since it actually has spinning platters that need to be powered. Nope. The My Passport draws right around 500mA consistently, which is what you expect for a physical hard drive. The ADATA, on the other hand, typically draws around 310mA, but every once in a while (and especially when you first connect it) it draws up to 1.35A! That's 1, 350mA, people! Or two My Passports, and more than half the way to a third! No wonder the hub crapped out and disconnected both of the drives! I did wonder if it might be the enclosure I used with the ADATA, but when I moved it to a different enclosure that worked with another SSD I have it did the same thing. Bottom Line: Not only is this drive pretty slow on write speeds, it draws a RIDICULOUS amount of power (albeit only sporadically) from the port it is connected to. Most USB hubs (with the exception of those plugged into mains power) are simply not going to support this kind of power draw. Neither will most USB ports on a laptop, even if you are plugging directly into the port. This drive may have a 2.5" form factor, but it's power draw puts it strictly in the desktop realm. Update: 6/21/2016 Honestly, I think I'd give them a zero, if I could. I went through their RMA process, and just got a replacement disk back. Formatted it for my Mac & then promptly ran BlackMagic on it. Read speeds are fairly consistent at 400+Mb/s, which is fine, but writes are a different story. The first 2 iterations were around 360 Mb/s, but then it tumbled over the next couple of iterations down to 80 Mb/s and stayed there. I finally stopped after about 20 iterations because at that point I was convinced it wouldn't get any better. It hasn't unmounted itself yet, but I've only been using it for 10 minutes. I won't be surprised if this one goes the same way as the last one. This is not what I thought I was getting into when I bought this. Guess it was on sale for a reason... At least it only cost me about 3 bucks to try the RMA process. Verdict: Fail. Update: 6/5/2016 The speed problems I reported below only got worse. Eventually the drive just stopped responding, and even managed to unmount itself. I contacted ADATA's customer support, and so far haven't found them to be helpful. I'm probably going to try to do an RMA and see if they can fix this, but I'm frankly not holding out much hope. They suggested I run their "SSD Toolbox" app, but when I went to their site I found it didn't support the drive I bought! Wonderful! My suggestion: stay away from this one. I wish I'd spent just a few shekels more and gotten the SanDisk or the Samsung... Original Review: I bought the 480Gb version, and I'm not impressed. In my mind there are 2 reasons you buy a SSD: speed, and the fact that jostling the drive won't destroy it. This one fails on speed. I'm using it in an external enclosure attached to my MacBook Air. Out of curiosity I ran Blackmagic on it to see how fast it was. When I saw the results, I ran Blackmagic on everything I had to see if it was as bad as I thought. It was. Read speed is fairly consistent at about 400 Mb/s. Write speed is a different thing. My first 2 iterations in Blackmagic showed write speeds of 249 and 248 Mb/s. The 3rd showed 140 Mb/s. The next 9 runs kept the write speed in a tight bunch around 90 Mb/s. I ran 5 iterations of write/read tests on 6 other drives I have; 3 hard drives, 2 SSDs, and the internal SSD on my Mac. With the exception of the internal SSD, all 5 iterations on each drive were very tightly bunched, yielding very consistent write/read values. And the ONLY drive slower than this ADATA SSD for write speed was my 3-4 year old Western Digital 2 Tb My Passport. Both of my 3.5" hard drives beat it. Granted, the read speeds were very consistent around the 400 Mb/s mark, which is very fast (3-4 times faster than my spinning hard drives). But they were slower than my 2 Transcend SSDs (128Gb and 256Gb). And on write speeds the Transcends were 2 and 4 times as fast, respectively. I get that this is a budget SSD, but I'm thinking there are better ones to be had out there. Next time I'll stick with more of a name brand.

full_text: tiny! great for a custom Linux-based wifi router My first one was DOA with bent RAM slot pins. CompuLab/Fitlet didn't reply to my RMA request, so I did a return with Amazon. New one works great and has zero manufacturing flaws. You MUST use 1.35V LOW VOLTAGE RAM / DDR3L. Regular DDR3 will fit but will not work. Fitment in the RAM slot is awkward, you must find the correct angle and it should slide in easily. I'm using Kingston 8GB PC3L part# KVR16LS11/8 with zero issues. I'm not sure how much is supported, but reports say upwards of 32GB. Includes an American Megatrends BIOS, hit DEL to get into the settings pre-boot. These run a little HOT but that's totally normal for a passively-cooled CPU (they rarely have failure risks with high heat). Make sure you use the heat spreader plate for the mSATA SSD card. It bolts down between the mSATA card and WIFI card using one of the mSATA mounting screws. The included instruction guide (10 pages) does not mention it at all. Also not mentioned is the BIOS reset button, which can be found on the board near the corner opposite the SIM card slot. Hold for 5 seconds to reset the BIOS to defaults. Fitlet has a Wiki with lots of information not included in the manual! UPDATE: About a week into it running 24/7; the heat caused the plastic "lens" in the power button (the part that refracts the green/orange light) to literally pop out. Only cosmetic but wacky either way. I purchased a 3rd party heatsink cover with large fins to replace the stock aluminum cover and lower temperatures by 10+ degrees F.

full_text: I almost liked this product but... My Motorola T505 has served me well for years and still works fine but I am getting tired asking folks to wait while I search for another clear FM station as the miles tick by. Therefore I was and still am looking for a Bluetooth hands free device that plugs into my aux port. After a lot of research and reading reviews I decided to try the Himbox HB01. I expected I would need an extension cable and adaptor for the audio because my aux in is not on the dash and is dual RCA instead of a mini phone jack. No problem finding the adapter and a shielded extension at a reasonable price so I ordered them at the same time. Once I had all the pieces I excitedly plugged it all together and turned on the power. Following the instructions, the device paired immediately with my phone. The first thing I tried was playing some music. Surprise number one was that I had to really turn up the volume to get to a normal/comfortable listening level. I guess I can live with that BUT with the volume up that high, there was an annoying electrical noise, during low volume and silent portions of the music. It is the ticketing and alternator whine anyone who has ever done any automotive audio work knows all too well. At normal volume settings it was almost inaudible but at the needed setting it was very annoying. Thinking perhaps the output level of the HB01 was abnormally low (defective device?) I reached out to tech support. They suggested an isolator in the audio line might solve the problem. Fortunately by the time I got the response I had deduced the same thing myself and had already ordered an isolation transformer. While waiting for it I decided to test the phone call quality. The good news was that the volume level was much better when using the phone than playing music, so the whine was less annoying. Unfortunately, again, I was told by a couple of folks I called to test, that my voice sounded muffled, I decided I would wait and try a few different mic locations after I got the isolator. To make an long story longer, a few days later I received the isolator and put it in line with the audio extension. BEAUTIFULL! It did exactly what it was supposed to do. No more whine or ticking even with the he volume control at maximum. I put on some more music and it was clean. Now to find out where the microphone wants to be. It will probably be best on the dash panel directly in front of me and behind the steering wheel. I stuck it there, neatened up the wires, and powered it up again. Everything was working fine so time to try another phone call... wait... the blue light just went out. Something just broke. 20 minutes on time and something died. I noticed the light in the power adapter was out too, so I unplugged it and pulled out the USB plug. I plugged it back in and it lit up. Plugged in the USB connector it went out. Thinking it might be the power adapter I decided to try another (I have several). Same thing. Plug in the HB01, it does not come on and the light on the power adapter goes out. Clearly something is shorted in the unit itself. Back to tech support, I explained the issue via email. Another 24 hours waiting for a response. The good news is they immediatley issued me an RMA and a pickup tag with which to send back the unit. They promised to send me a new one as soon as they received the old one. full_text: Newer models seem lacking in quality I live in an older house and neighborhood with old overhead power lines and transformers. Voltage sags when people run their air conditioners and these units work well for boosting voltage. I own six of the older model SS1200 which has the rectangular case. The newer ones have a trapezoidal-shaped case. I have not had any problems with the older models, but I would have to say that the capacity is rather low and it is worthwhile to consider the SS2000 if you're planning to plug in more than 5.5A total draw. The SS2000 uses the same case and has a heavier-gauge power cord, although it still seems to be the bare minimum for the rated 9.1A. However, I ordered 2 of the newer SS2000s and had problems with both (see my review of the SS2000 for details). The last SS1200 that I bought had a cracked rear panel but is still safe to use as the crack is in the mounting hole. This is due to how these units are packaged and handled during shipment. The cord and plug are packaged at the back of the unit, and if it's dropped during shipment on the back panel, the weight of the transformer causes the plug to crack the panel. I suspect that the type of polymer used in the case has changed. Also, if you get a lemon, Amazon cannot take these units back even though they are not a UPS and do not contain a lead-acid battery. Amazon sent a replacement, but after the second one was also a lemon, they referred me to the manufacterer which I would have to RMA and send back for repair at my cost.

full_text: Believe It Or Not, A Real Workhorse Travel Case I work in the IT field, and I use my portable hard drive many times a day, every day of the week. It lives in my back pack. I'm looking for speed and reliability. And this is my favorite portable hard drive enclosure. Yes, the basic enclosure is plastic and the covers are thin metal and they look cheaply made, But this is my second SIIG and I purchased it only because my first one was SATA II and I wanted SATA III. The first one is still working flawlessly and has lasted longer than any other enclosure I've tried (well over a year), and I have a whole drawer full of cases that didn't cut it. This is because IT USES A TYPE-A CONNECTOR where the cable plugs into the enclosure! Most USB 3.0 and 3.1 drive enclosures use the type-B connector and they are so flimsy that they fail within weeks unless you are extremely careful in how you plug the cable into the enclosure, whereas a the metal part of a type-A connector is about twice as long as a type-B so it sticks further into the enclosure and about 3x higher so fits much tighter (see picture- left is type-A, right is type-B). I can pick up the enclosure with a mechanical HD in it by the cable and it stays plugged in. When I'm done using it, I just toss it into my backpack with the cable still connected and never have had any problem with it. I previously bought 2 Ank** metal enclosures with the standard type-B cable connectors. Both failed at the case connector and Ank** replaced them. The new ones failed, and Ank** sent me just the internal circuit board with the connect on it. I then drilled and tapped the heavy metal case covers so I could screw on a metal brace and Ty-rapped the cable connector to the brace and they lasted a little longer. Then I found the SIIG case and have never had a single instance of the cable falling out or the case socket bending so it would no longer retain the cable plug. I also have had to RMA several drives because they got hosed-up when the connection failed during writes to the drive... until I got the SIIG cases. They are the best out there.

full_text: Way Better Than I Expected These replaced the non-working stock rear speakers in a 1999 Chevy Silverado extended cab and they sound way better than I ever expected, even with the factory head unit. I had already replaced the front speakers with a set of somewhat high-end 6.5-inch component speakers from another manufacturer, and I wanted speakers for the back with a similar sensitivity to balance the sound output in the cab. These were the ONLY 4 x 6 speakers I could find with the same sensitivity rating they would not have been my first choice, and I contemplated sending them back when I opened the box because the build quality was noticeably lower than the speakers I installed up front. These speakers don't fit the factory speaker holes in the truck. The factory speakers are glued onto plastic mounting clips that act as spacers, so I ended up ripping the old speakers off the factory mounting clips and then attaching these speakers to those plastic brackets. Near as I can tell, this is the only way to get the speakers to fit without making the factory holes bigger. Before I installed the speakers, I plugged them in and listened to them and was TOTALLY unimpressed. They sounded flat and tinny. To my surprise, when they were installed in the truck, they took on a totally different sound quality. The sheetmetal in the extended cab area of the truck acts as a baffle and these little speakers put out an intense amount of bass as well as a very sharp high-end. They put off so much bass they rattle the trim panels with the original 1999 GM head unit! I was able to adjust the EQ to stop the rattles, but still maintain a full, deep tone. The small tweeter also produces a bright, crisp high-end sound. I mainly listen to classic rock, jazz, talk radio / podcasts, and oldies. These speakers sound great with everything I've thrown at them. Going from front-only to having both front and rear speakers, it really makes the music I listen to in my old truck come alive. It's not a high-end, high-performance sound, but it's way better than I thought my beat up old Chevy pickup would ever sound and I don't regret buying these one bit.

full_text: Great wireless access point as part of an enterprise-grade a-la-carte home or small-office networking setup I purchased this access point hoping it would be the only one I needed, but with the knowledge that if I needed more than one, it would be easy to build a meshed network of these APs to achieve ideal coverage in my home. As it turned out, my 1600 sq ft home sitting on a .15 acre lot is easily covered by this AP. I have this AP mounted on the ceiling of my second floor hallway of my house, as near to the center of the house as I could reasonably achieve, and it is working very well. I get a strong signal even outdoors to the edges of my property line and a little beyond. I can't say whether the Pro was necessary in my case or if the Lite would have sufficed, as I started with the Pro. I do feel like, though, that if I had chosen the Lite, I probably would have needed more than one, which would have increased my installation time/complexity and cost me more than the single Pro. So, I think the added cost for the Pro was, in my case, worth it. The setup & control software is a bit more complicated, but still workable. It's odd that you have to run the control software server from your computer to configure the APs, but at least you need not leave that server software running at all times just for the AP to work; you only need to have the server running all the time if you want to use certain features such as the temporary access guest network with splash screen login (like what you find at Starbucks or many hotels). The device itself is very attractive, sleek, and low-profile, so even my very aesthetic-conscious wife was not upset by this new device I attached to our ceiling. I initially figured I'd have to disable to the blue LED light emanating from it, but we found it is actually quite helpful due to the placement in our upstairs hallway; it serves as a wonderful nightlight--just bright enough to see by, but not so much to be annoying or distracting even if we leave the bedroom door open. Take note of the item you receive to ensure you are receiving a truly new item. I was highly disappointed with Amazon with the first device that was shipped to me, as it was very obviously a used/returned item, with a broken seal to the box and missing the slipcover on the box, subtle but visible wear to the logo on the device, and shoddy/missing packaging (mounting screws missing, cords not properly wrapped up, some items not wrapped in plastic that should have been and place in the box in the wrong locations, and even an empty bag that I later realized was supposed to have contained those missing mounting screws). I didn't even install that item, but instead sent it back and had a new one shipped. The new one was obviously new, properly sealed and packaged, with all contents included and in pristine shape. I hope this is not an indicator of a shift in Amazon's fulfillment practices, selling used/returned items at new prices, or I will have to seriously rethink my Prime membership...

full_text: Cost-effective solution to the problem of weak networking signals Very simple, but also not quite as plug and play as they would have you believe. I have a great router, but the signal weakens upstairs at the opposite end of the house. So much so that some of my wifi-connected devices disconnect from time to time. This promises to be the answer to that, and to a degree, it is. It is very simple, and allows few adjustments by the user. They also don't give you much advice for how to set it up in the best way. It takes one of your existing wifi bands, either 2.4 or 5GHz (but not both), and repeats it onto separate channels at 2.4 or 5GHz. I decided to use my 5GHz band as the existing one because it is faster but doesn't travel as far or as well through walls as the 2.4 band. I made sure I placed the product close enough to the router so it got a good signal, which was easy because it has a strength meter on the front. It picked up that band and retransmitted it as 2.4 and 5GHz signals with separate SSIDs (network ID names). Anything that uses the new retransmitted signal will lose bandwidth (speed) because of the overhead required to retransmit it using the same radios used to receive it. This is to increase range, not speed, though a strong signal with half the bandwidth is generally faster than a weak one at full bandwidth. Your mileage may vary. It did work, but I found the separate SSIDs to be annoying. To connect to it, I had to do so deliberately by selecting it. For internet-connected devices that don't move around, this is less of a problem as they can be set to use the new SSID and left that way. Theoreticallly, it is possible to set everything to the same SSID and have the devices themselves automatically connect to the strongest signal. In real life, however, I found that this resulted in things not connecting at all along with dropped connections as I moved around the house. The very limited FAQ that D-Link provides for the product on their web site addresses this by basically saying not to do it. I agree with this, at least for the devices in my home. Plus, if you set everything to the same SSID and have troubles, it becomes very difficult to change them back. I had to take down my main network to ensure I was connected to the D-Link directly, and it still was so difficult I ended up doing a factory reset on it to get it back. (There is a small pinhole on the right side, if you insert a paper clip or SIM ejector and press for 30 seconds it will reset it.) One last thing. In the pictures, this looks like a nice, neat thing that plugs in and looks great. I found that it is rather tall and heavy enough so that it leans forward in the socket, especially since there is no ground pin to help stabilize it. This made it look rather saggy. I tried plugging it in upside-down, and while this cured the sagging problem, also made it look kind of silly and may have even reduced the range a bit as the antennas were closer to the floor level. I found a place behind an end table that worked pretty well. It was mostly hidden, but also not covered up, which might affect its performance. Just something to keep in mind. In the end, this is an okay solution to a problem. I'll probably end up replacing it with a mesh networking solution, but in the meantime, this will buy me some time for those to improve and the costs to come down a bit. Recommended, but know why you are buying it and what it will do (and not do) for you. Sean Logue, 2017

full_text: So good, I bought another UPDATED REVIEW 9/17/16: This is the second set I've bought. I lost the first set and it was rock solid. Amazing battery life that literally lasted me 8 hours+ straight, so I had no problem using this all day for work or music playback. I love the fact that you get told how much battery life the unit has when you first power it on. The sound is great for the price. I really can't complain. I can make calls to my last dialed call with the phone button and I and receive calls by pressing the phone icon button. Calls are clear and the mic is good enough that others can also hear my clearly on the other end. The reception range is fair, but not great. I'd say you'll get about 20-30 feet before the unit has connectivity problems so if your phone is stationary and you're walking around, try to stay in that range. Walls and elevation (stairs) will also affect the reception. This is a no frills unit that just works and is an overall great value. I had the option to try a different bluetooth headphone set but the SoundPeats Universal Q800 was so satisfying and such a value for the price that I knew I could not go wrong with getting another set. It comes in cardboard packaging with a micro usb charging cable, 3 different sized earpiece attachments, and a simple manual. Pairing the headset with my phone was simple. If you need to enter a code, just put 0000 into your phone once it finds this headset. When you have the earbuds on, you'll hear a female voice say "Power on. Battery level (high, medium, low). You're headset is connected." I love this feature. When you turn off the Q800, it'll say, "Power off." Simple and very effective. The earbuds store easily into the headset with magnetic slots. You get 3 different sets of sizes so you can find the size the fits you best. The default size that came on the headset was perfectly comfortable for my tastes. The headset itself is quite comfortable resting around my neck. It took a little getting used to my first time because I wasn't used to wearing anything around my neck, but once my body got used to the feeling of something touching my neck all the time, it felt like second nature. I'd say that the adjustment took me about a day. Your mileage may vary. The rubber band around the headset is flexible. The controls are quite large, which is nice, because I am able to feel the symbols and can tell which button I am pushing. The phone icon also lights up and blinks when you first turn on the headset. When pressing the volume button to lower or raise the volume, you'll hear a beep to indicate that you've pressed the button. With the headset on, the volume buttons are on your right, next to the power button, which is located on the inside side of the headset where the USB charging port is (covered by a protective rubber flap). The left side has a skip previous button, skip next track button, and pause/play button. Sadly, you can't fast forward or fast rewind your tracks. The left side buttons have a lower double tone and the right side buttons have a higher pitched beep tone each time you depress them. Interestingly enough, the left side buttons will only beep if you press them for more than a second, but the volume buttons will always beep each time you press them. If your volume is maxed out to the loudest or lowest level, you'll get one long beep. When your volume is maxed out, the lowest volume indication beep is a low-pitched tone and the highest volume indication beep is a higher pitched tone. When charging the headset, the phone icon is read and when the battery level is fully charged, the icon turns blue. The phone icon will periodically blink blue every 5 seconds to indicate that the unit is on and in use. There was a lot of thought put into designing the interface of this device. SUMMARY: PROS: -Easy to pair -Amazing battery life of 8+ hours continuous usage -Comfortable earbuds -Flexible and comfortable neckband -Magnetic earbuds for easy storage of earbuds -LED phone icon to indicate unit is on. -Large control icons -Verbal battery volume indicator -Verbal power on and power off indicator -Average connected distance of 20-30 feet -Clear phone calls CONS: -No ability to fast forward or rewind tracks

full_text: The best I've found to date I'll start by saying the headset I'm reviewing was as a replacement for another MPow headset. At the time of this writing, the customer service is excellent. I had issues with the other headset, while this set... not so much. The replacement was free of charge, so if you find that one of their headsets isn't working for you, contact them and see what they can do. The comfort on this headset is very good. The wires are moldable so they wrap around your ears and I do worry about metal fatigue setting in and causing problems later in the life of this headset but if something happens, I'll come back and update the review. The ear buds fit directly in the ear canals and have some flexibility in the angle so these should work well as long as you have no problems with little rubber pieces sealing up your ability to hear. With them fully inserted, even with nothing coming out of them, the outside world is very far away. (If you require feedback from your voice to determine how loud to be, expect to be yelling a lot...) The sound is very good and appears to be full range. I have to keep my volume very low to keep from hurting my ear drums but if you need to apply a little pressure, expect these to crank out the sound. I have no problems being heard when I'm making a phone call even when there is quite a bit of ambient noise around me. No complaints on call quality from the other end of the line. It takes about 2 hours for a full charge and at the volume level I use, I was able to listen to music for 16 hours before I got the low battery warning. The buttons work as expected though they are a smidge close to the ear and quite close together. (This would be the only thing I wouldn't mind seeing changed. The controls should be far enough down that they can be seen easily.) Single presses to the volume up and down adjust the volume accordingly on my android smartphone. I haven't played much with the other button presses as I prefer to control the music directly from my phone. Overall, this is the best headset I've picked up over the last few weeks (5 total over 4 weeks. The next best set only lasted 4 hours of play time so I would need two of them to be able to last a full day. Others has issues with sound, comfort, or flexibility.) I'm ending my search with this pair as it seems to be exactly what I want. *Update 5/23/16* I've been playing with these for two months now. It took about 3 weeks for the battery to drop from the initial 16 hours to the stated amount. (I'm actually getting closer to 8 1/2 instead of the stated 7 so it's still doing well.) I use them nearly every day on multiple devices but haven't gotten them to work on multiple devices at the same time. It's not a big part of why I wanted them so I haven't sought out tech support on them. But keep it in mind if this is a reason for you purchasing them. No fatigue on the ear wire yet so things are still good there. I'll update if that changes. Overall, my initial review stands. These are a good pair of headphones if you like the in-ear over the ear style.

There is better interface software out there, but everything is pretty much plug and play with a default setup that will get you up and running with very little effort. I left default settings for resolution and set it up to record on motion triggers and the buffer lasts more than 10 days with a 2TB drive and almost constant triggering from one of our exterior cameras. Addendum: Nick made good on issuing another headphone. This one works. Concerning the phones themselves: I used to play keyboard(s) in a dance band and have been in recording studios (ancient history) so I have some idea as to sound characteristics/issues. When you see technicians in the studio running wires from millions of dollars of equipment to crappy 2 inch speakers you begin to understand that they were in a no win situation for having to satisfy both high-end and low end users. The studios made compromises also and unless you have access to the master tapes you are stuck with their own compromises as to sound. This was true when the medium was vinyl records where the first pass with the needle was the best sound you could get because the grooves that had the higher frequencies were stripped out faster, the tapes that built up oxides and heads that had to be cleaned constantly with tape wear and tear and breakage, to digital CD and flash drives. The weakest part of the chain was always the speaker. It was either too good for the medium or too bad (sometimes because it was too good and would pick up the artifacts). From my perspective, I can see the use of top of the line headphones when editing the master tapes but I have reservations about the effectiveness of using the same when you at the end of the listening chain with all the issues involved with it, from studio to method of transmission and age of recording. All of that affects or degrades the signal. You don't need a Ferrari to go 55 mph on a U.S. highway. Frequency of range is nice for a stat but once you are past being a teenager you start losing the ability to hear the higher end. Pros: the drivers on this thing are massive; phones are fairly light weight; FM is acceptable (actually I'm amending that now-I'm in a fringe reception area and it's pretty good considering-not anywhere as good as my Tivoli, but hardly anything is); excellent battery life. Not Pro or Con: out of the box the bias is toward the bass, but not outrageously so; the genre of music you listen to may determine whether you like it or not. Cons: middle and high-end range is not as balanced with the bass as some would like, and I can't disagree with that; unit itself is somewhat fragile so don't go throwing it at a wall or sit on it; on more sophisticated/complex music tracks there are "separation" issues between various instruments. With all that said these are the best you can get at this price range and are way better than some of the more expensive ones with its drivers. My assumption is that the company took advantage of the massive drivers to deliver the bass to younger listeners and the genres they listen to as they may be the majority buyers. I don't object to the lack of some "tightness" in the sound some have complained about as that compensates to a certain extent for the artifacts that come from weaknesses inherent in Bluetooth and FM transmissions. Sometimes speakers can be "too good" for receiving transmissions. My own tastes are pretty eclectic, running from classical, jazz and country to rock and heavy metal. Despite its weaknesses with some of them I'm fine with how the phones generally operate with these different genres at the price point. If they break I have no problems ordering a new inexpensive one. My take: if an inexpensive speaker setup has to be biased in favor of a set of frequencies I will pick bass. For myself, headphones that are biased toward middle and high ranges are impossible to listen to. I can't stand a "tinny" sound. full_text: Great mids and highs. These in-ceiling speakers are fantastic. They're very easy to install and come with a good template for cutting in walls or ceilings. I wouldn't recommend the wire that comes with it. It's quite thin. Here's my tips for ceiling mounting: -take one of the templates and find the center. Put a nail through the center. When you have a place where you think you want the speaker, nail up the template. This way you can step back and see if it's in the right spot. Draw around the template with pencil and take the template off. -always check what's behind your drywall when cutting into a ceiling or wall! -use a sharp jab saw to cut out the circular template you've drawn onto the ceiling. Cut just outside the line. The speaker has a lip, so don't be too afraid. Cutting inside the template will make it really difficult to put the speaker into the ceiling. -use a drop cloth or a large garbage bags just under your cutting surface to catch the drywall when cutting. -gently push the screws from the back and the speaker grill will pop out. -test fit the speaker in the hole! It should just fit without forcing, but definitely not super loose. The hole should be completely covered by the lip. Then pull it back out. -while the speaker is out, you can pull your speaker wire through the hole and either add wore harnesses to slip on the speaker's tabs or solder directly. Doing it while outside of the ceiling will make it much easier than crouching in a hot attic. Trust me. -put everything back through the hole and screw it down. You can use a drill, but the screws should be hand tight, not so right it breaks the plastic! Add a powered subwoofer and a nice receiver and you have yourself a very nice speaker system!

full_text: Solid drive so far After facing a seagate drive failure, I purchased this at a local big-box store. Initial impressions are very good. The enclosure feels fairly solid for plastic, the cord is the perfect length (roughly 1'), and plug into the drive with satisfying firmness. The enclosure itself is extremely small, looking at it compared to a traditional 2.5" drive, I'm not sure how they fit it and a controller in there, but I digress. Now, on to the drive itself. One thing I would like to clear up, right off the bat: This is a hard drive. Hard drives fail. These are not permanent storage mediums, nay, an array of hard drives is something that should always be backed up and duplicated. Data you don't have in more than two locations is data you don't care about. With that said, this was purchased to replace my main working drive for photo and (light) video editing. I work with lots and lots of RAW files (current library is over 37,000), so I naturally needed a big and fast drive. I formatted this using exFAT, so I can hop between Mac, Windows, and Linux. Black magic Disk Speed Test reveals roughly 110MBps on read and write, which is excellent for such a compact drive. Drive mounts immediately and does not unmount unexpectedly. File transfers are zippy, and do not slow overtime. The drive does get slightly warm to the touch, but nothing out of the ordinary. I cannot comment on long-term reliability, but WD and HGST both have reputations for producing reliable drives, as BackBlaze's hard drive reliability assessment confirms. All-in-all, a great drive for a great price. Would buy again (and probably will). Edit: After a couple months of usage, the drive failed. I was able to get an RMA really easily and the replacement only took a few weeks. This new drive has been much better to me, although the USB cord looks like it is getting very weak where it meets the connectors. Nothing major but minus one star for having a drive fail after a few months.

full_text: It works. I used the Evercool fan to replace the factory one in the Tivo Roamio OTA DVR. After installation, I put all of the screws back and re-attached the cover and powered the Tivo on. I heard the fan whirring for 30 seconds or so, then it went silent. Because the air it displaces is minimal, it was difficult to confirm that it continued to run after this. I was tempted to take the cover off again to check. But it had been a pain to take it off and put it back on (normal for the first time) that I decided to wait. By wetting a finger and holding it near the right side vent as you are facing the front of the DVR, you can feel the slightest evaporation. The air intake vent on the left side actually feels slightly cool compared to the right exhaust vent which becomes markedly warm. So, to avoid this uncertainty, I recommend that after you install the fan, but before replacing all of the screws and the cover, power the unit on to check the fans operation. As others have suggested, installing the top two screws seems to provide enough holding power to keep the fan firmly in place. This will make replacing the fan easier the next time. A worthwhile step, pre-installation, is to twist the screws that hold the fan in place into the fan to cut the threads. The original fan began making noise after about five months, and based on many comments about this fan, I expect I will have to replace it many times over the life of the Roamio OTA. The time and money involved to do this repair is certainly modest and will save you from all the time you would probably have to spend dealing with Tivos customer service and the fact that they would require you to send it to them for repair, with the possible loss of everything you have recorded, and the inconvenience of being without it for however long it would take them to send it back to you. Tools required: Torx drivers #8,10, and 15. Ten and Fifteen are fairly common for car repair. You likely already have them in your tool box. Eight is rather small. I had to go the the hardware store to buy one. ($3.60). A small flat head screwdriver helps to pry the cover offthe hardest part of this repair, really. My fingernails just couldn't provide enough leverage to do it. Just go slowly and carefully. You don't want to accidentally jab the motherboard with the screwdriver. A pair of needle nose pliers can be used to start the nut on the coaxial connector (antenna), but a 13mm socket fits it perfectly and speeds removal and replacement. A deep 13mm socket makes it even easier to do by hand. A small Phillips head driver completes the repair kit. Theres a great How-to video on YouTube that will guide you through the repair. The next time, if youve installed the fan with just the top two screws, the Torx #15 will be the only tool you truly must have, though youll likely want to use the screwdriver again to pry the cover off. IMPORTANT NOTE: This information is for the Tivo Roamio OTA only. The Tivo Roamio designed to work with cable TV has an additional step required--the removal of the cable card and the cable card assembly. This must be done before the motherboard can be removed.

The customer service guy did say that usually this issue is caused by an EDID handshake error caused by an adapter or some configuration issue. When the monitor doesn't get the correct response from the computer it freezes and will do nothing until the power is pulled. The reason I think it is the power supply is because I had another monitor doing the same thing many years ago that the manufacturer diagnosed as a faulty power supply. It could totally be this EDID thing, though - in which case I would argue that the monitor should have some kind of fault tolerance built in so it doesn't just die if it doesn't get the right response.
